summary: The only pod in payments/checkout-api (checkout-api-7f87c646c6-h6mj8) is in CrashLoopBackOff because its container command is hardcoded to print "FATAL: DATABASE_URL not set" and exit 1, so it fails on every start whatever the environment. The pod named in the alert (checkout-api-7d9f8c6b5-x2kq9, container checkout-api) does not exist, and the alert's start time (09:14Z) is about 5 hours before the current deployment was created (~14:25Z), so the alert is stale, from another cluster, or from an earlier deleted copy of this deployment. checkout-api has 0 available replicas and no Endpoints object named checkout-api was found, so it is serving nothing here; this is SEV2 if this is production payments, lower if it is a test or sandbox cluster.
verified_facts: The alerted pod payments/checkout-api-7d9f8c6b5-x2kq9 returns NotFound for both describe and logs.

The pod's single container is named 'busybox' (not 'checkout-api'), image busybox:1.36.
The container command is: sh -c 'echo FATAL: DATABASE_URL not set >&2; exit 1'. It always exits 1 and checks no environment variable.

Previous container logs contain only: 'FATAL: DATABASE_URL not set'.
The container has no environment variables set (Environment: <none>) and no volumes apart from the service account token.

Deployment status: 1 desired, 0 available; condition Available=False (MinimumReplicasUnavailable).
The image pulled successfully; there are no scheduling, image-pull, OOMKilled or probe-failure events. The only warnings are BackOff (x37 over 35m).

No Endpoints object named checkout-api exists in payments.
assumptions: Kubernetes describe output shows +0530 timestamps; I assumed these convert to ~14:25Z, which I compared with the alert's 09:14Z start.
I assumed the cluster I queried is the one the alert came from; the different pod name, container name and timing suggest it may not be.
I did not check whether a Service with a different name selects app=checkout-api, or whether an Ingress or upstream callers depend on it.
I assumed 'payments' may be a production payment path, which drives the SEV2 rating; if this is a test or sandbox cluster, SEV3/4 is more appropriate.
I did not check whether a ConfigMap or Secret holding DATABASE_URL exists in the namespace.

hypotheses.cause: The deployment spec is broken or a placeholder: the container command is hardcoded to print a FATAL message and exit 1, and the image is generic busybox rather than a real checkout-api image. It will crash loop whatever the environment.
evidence: The command is literally 'echo FATAL: DATABASE_URL not set >&2; exit 1'. It checks no variable and always exits 1.
Image is busybox:1.36 and the container is named 'busybox', unlike the 'checkout-api' container named in the alert.
Exit code 1 within the same second as start; logs contain only the FATAL line.
Revision 1 with no previous ReplicaSet: the spec has never run successfully.
diagnostic_commands: kubectl get deployment checkout-api -n payments -o yaml
kubectl get deployment checkout-api -n payments -o jsonpath='{.metadata.managedFields}'

hypotheses.cause: Missing DATABASE_URL configuration, taking the log message at face value: the intended checkout-api deployment should inject DATABASE_URL from a Secret or ConfigMap, and the manifest that was applied leaves it out.
evidence: The log says DATABASE_URL not set, and the container has no env, envFrom or volumes.
Weakened: the command exits 1 unconditionally, so adding DATABASE_URL would not stop the crash in this spec.

hypotheses.cause: The alert is stale or mis-routed: it refers to a pod (ReplicaSet hash 7d9f8c6b5, container checkout-api) from an earlier, deleted deployment or a different cluster, and the current crash loop would fire its own separate alert.
evidence: The alerted pod is NotFound; the only ReplicaSet is 7f87c646c6 and there are no old ReplicaSets.
Alert startsAt 09:14Z is ~5h before the current deployment was created at ~14:25Z.
Container name in the alert (checkout-api) differs from the actual container (busybox).

safe_next_actions: Find out who created or applied payments/checkout-api about 35 minutes ago (GitOps/CI history, audit logs, managedFields) and whether the busybox placeholder command was deliberate.

Get the intended checkout-api manifest from source control and compare it with the live spec: kubectl get deployment checkout-api -n payments -o yaml. Expect differences in image, command, and DATABASE_URL env/secretRef.
Confirm which cluster and Prometheus instance sent the alert (pod 7d9f8c6b5-x2kq9, container checkout-api, start 09:14Z), since it does not match this cluster's state.
Check whether anything depends on checkout-api here (kubectl get svc,ingress -n payments) to confirm customer impact and set the final severity.

Owners should then redeploy the correct manifest through the normal pipeline (real image, no hardcoded exit, DATABASE_URL from a Secret), or scale the deployment to 0 if it is an unintended test, to stop alert noise.
rollback_plan: The implicated change is the creation of deployment payments/checkout-api about 35 minutes ago (revision 1). There is no earlier revision, so `kubectl rollout undo` will not work.
